report.summary: One action-required phantom control: POST /login rate limiting is still modeled as implemented, but its middleware now passes every request through without limiting.

findings.title: Implemented login rate-limiting control is now a pass-through

evidence.note: The updated comment only says the function wraps the login handler chain and no longer claims enforcement.
RateLimit remains defined but contains no rate-limiting logic.
The middleware returns the next handler directly, so requests are never limited.

relevance.justification: Strong: the changed implementation directly removes the behavior backing a control explicitly marked implemented.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: in threat "credential stuffing", the control "login rate limiting" at line 17 is marked implemented = true and claims a per-IP token-bucket middleware in internal/auth/ratelimit.go, but this PR replaces RateLimit with a pass-through that returns next directly (internal/auth/ratelimit.go:6-7). Set implemented = false and revise the description to state that rate limiting is currently absent, or restore the per-IP token-bucket implementation before retaining implemented = true.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the "login rate limiting" control to implemented = false and update its description, or restore the claimed per-IP token-bucket middleware.
